intent: Specify the `tinyset::set64::Fits64` implementations (`to_u64` and `from_u64`) for `u64`, `u32`, `u16`, `u8`, `usize`, `i8`, `i16`, `i32`, `i64` and `isize`.

manual_mutants.note: negative value computed from the unshifted word
large non-negative i64 decoded through 32 bits

sibling_mutants.after: ok (if x.val < 2^32 then UScalar.cast .U32 x else 0#u32)
sibling_mutants.note: out-of-domain words (never produced by to_u64) decode to 0 instead of truncating
decoder only looks at the low 9 bits (enough for every i8 encoding)

bug_variants.source: https://github.com/droundy/tinyset/commit/25c415bed91bac37bccf6470ff60d055d4548449 ("fix a bug in my Fits64 implementation for minimum negative integers")
bug_variants.note: pre-fix signed Fits64 (tinyset 0.4.1) encodes `(self.abs() << 1) + sign_bit`: `abs()` overflows on the minimum value (i8::MIN, ..., i64::MIN, isize::MIN), so to_u64 panics instead of being the documented infallible, lossless conversion and the test_fits64 round trip fails there (the old sign-magnitude decoder `abs*(neg*(-2)+1)` also maps words 0 and 1 both to 0, so the encoding is not a bijection on the type's words); the extracted `core.mem.size_of::<Self>()` call (an opaque external in Aeneas) is replaced by its constant value (1/2/4/8/8 bytes)

edits.with_text:
def I8.Insts.TinysetSet64Fits64.to_u64 (self : Std.I8) : RustM Std.U64 := do
  let i ← core.num.I8.abs self
  let i1 ← lift (IScalar.hcast .U64 i)
  let a ← i1 <<< 1#i32
  let i2 ← lift (IScalar.hcast .U8 self)
  let i3 ← ok 1#usize
  let i4 ← 8#usize * i3
  let i5 ← i4 - 1#usize
  let i6 ← i2 >>> i5
  let b ← lift (UScalar.cast .U64 i6)
  a + b
